question: What does the idiom 'Get to the point' mean?
solution:
The correct answer is: **Option 1** i.e. **Speak directly**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The idiom **"Get to the point"** means to communicate clearly and directly, without unnecessary details or digressions. (मुद्दे पर आना)

 
 
• **Example: **The meeting is running long, so please get to the point and share your main idea.
 
 
 
• **"Speak directly"** means to talk in a straightforward, clear, and concise manner, addressing the main subject without unnecessary elaboration. (सीधे बात करना)
 
 
• **Example: **When giving feedback, it’s better to speak directly rather than beating around the bush.
 
 
 
• Hence, the idiom **'Get to the point' **aligns with **'Speak directly'**.

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Option 1 - Speak directly**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **Interrupt **(बात काटना): To stop someone from speaking by saying or doing something.

 
 
• **Example:** Please don’t interrupt when someone else is speaking.
 
 
 
• **Avoid the matter **(मुद्दे को टालना): To deliberately refrain from addressing the subject at hand.
 
 
• **Example: **He tried to avoid the matter by changing the topic.
 
 
 
• **Speak indirectly** (अप्रत्यक्ष रूप से बात करना): To communicate in a roundabout way without addressing the issue directly.
 
 
• **Example:** Instead of speaking indirectly, it’s better to be honest and transparent.
 
 

5f:Tbf6,
The correct answer is **Option 1**.<
